Work on the data of a cohort and keep its exclusion table

Source: R/cohort_data.R
cohort_data.Rd

cohort_data() gives the data of a cohort::CohortPipeline after its exclusions. keep_exclusions() puts the exclusion table of the pipeline on the value of a step after the cohort, such as an imputation.

Usage

cohort_data(cp)

keep_exclusions(x, cp)

Arguments

cp

A cohort::CohortPipeline after its exclusions.

x

The value of the step after the cohort, any R object other than NULL. For example a data.table, a list of imputed data sets or a mids object.

Value

cohort_data(): a data.table. keep_exclusions(): x with the attributes pbn_exclusions and pbn_n_before.

Details

A step after the cohort reads the data with cohort_data(). As the step after_cohort of add_data(), it returns its value, and pbn puts the exclusion table on it:

data_impute <- function(cp) {
  d <- pbn::cohort_data(cp)
  lapply(1:5, function(k) impute_once(d))
}

At the end of a data function fn, the step returns pbn::keep_exclusions(imp, cp), so that the table stays.

cohort_data() returns cp$get_included(<cohort>). <cohort> is the one cohort of the pipeline that no other cohort branches from, the cohort that add_data() gives the analyses. It stops on a pipeline with more than one such cohort.

keep_exclusions() returns x with two attributes. pbn_exclusions holds the exclusion table of cp, and pbn_n_before holds cp$n_total(), the number of rows given to the pipeline. The analyses get x, and save_results() writes the table to the element exclusions. The section A cohort as the data of add_data() gives the columns.

For a value that is not a data.frame, the check of run_plan() for an analysis that changes the shared data in place checks nothing. manifest$n_rows_data is the number of rows of one data set when x is a list of data.frames with one number of rows, and NA otherwise.

A function that calls these two runs on each worker of run_plan(), so each worker needs pbn installed.

See also

vignette("pbn"), which imputes after the cohort.

Other plan: add_analyses(), add_data(), get_data(), progress(), run_plan()

Examples

d <- data.table::data.table(id = 1:6, age = c(15, 30, 41, 17, 52, 60))
cp <- cohort::CohortPipeline$new(d)
cp$exclude_and_track("root", "age under 18", "age < 18")
adults <- pbn::cohort_data(cp)
imp <- list(adults, adults)
attr(pbn::keep_exclusions(imp, cp), "pbn_exclusions")
#>   data         step n_before n_excluded n_after
#> 1 <NA> age under 18        6          2       4
